title: Music Generation — MusicGen, Stable Audio, Suno, and the Licensing Earthquake
service: MusicBox: symbolic prompt-to-notes generation, a SQLite track store with tempo maps, FAD scoring, bar-by-bar streaming to a player, and song-form expansion

parts.lesson_anchor: code/main.py fake_generate and its key, progression and drum tables; Exercise 1 (play the piece back as MIDI); Pitfall: tempo drift
planted_bugs: chord_tones checks endswith('m') before 'dim', so G#dim splits into the root 'G#di'; the KeyError surfaces one call down in note_number, two calls below render
parse_bpm is the lesson's token loop: '128 bpm' splits into two tokens and int('') is swallowed, so the tempo silently stays 120 and 8 bars come out as 16 s
seconds uses tick // PPQ, so every position inside a beat collapses onto the beat
_held_until rescans every rendered note for each chord tone, O(n^2)
parts.timing_assert: render of 2000 bars (about an hour at 140 bpm) under 0.15 s (quadratic version about 2.1 s, fixed version about 0.011 s)
parts.overfix_guard: the tempo is the number written before bpm ('8 bars of lofi at 90 bpm' is 90, not 8; 'jazz at 140BPM for 32 bars' is 140, not 32); legato survives the speed-up: D4 held over the repeated D chord, A4 held for three bars across the A and D chords, and a 16-bar D drone held from start to end, which rules out dropping legato, holding only when the whole chord repeats, and searching only the previous bar or the last N notes

parts.lesson_anchor: tokens over time on a tick grid; Pitfall: tempo drift; legal landscape: AI-generated music must be disclosed
parts.exactness: notes (integer ticks, in the given order), the tempo map (128, 140 and 400/3 bpm, as tuples) and the generation record (a 64-bit seed) round-trip exactly across close and reopen; seconds are derived from ticks through the tempo map

adjustments: Part 1: the suggested negative-transposition modulo bug was left out because Python's % already wraps negative semitones, so it would not be a natural Python bug here. The lesson's own BPM-parsing bug from code/main.py took its place, and the lesson's other bug (key detection by first letter) ships fixed with the quiz's regex so that Part 1 stays at four defects.

Part 1: the sixteenth-step defect is floor division in seconds() rather than an off-by-one. The lesson's drum patterns are 0-indexed strings, so an off-by-one step would have no natural cause in this code; floor division is the realistic slip in beat arithmetic, and it only shows on positions inside a beat.

Part 2: float seconds are kept out by design (ticks are stored, seconds derived through the tempo map) rather than by a failing round trip, because a seconds store that converts back with round() survives a round trip and only the truncating variant could be caught. The exactness assertion uses this domain's own precision traps instead: 140 bpm through MIDI's integer microseconds per quarter, 400/3 bpm, a 64-bit generation seed, tuple tempo pairs and note order. The lesson's disclosure rule (ai_generated) was added.

Part 4: Server-Sent Events, the push format a browser player reads. It differs from the NDJSON of 06/03, but 06/04, 06/05, 06/07, 06/08 and 06/12 also send SSE; what is particular to this part is the bar framing: notes cut at the bar line, tied over, and bars sent until the last note ends.
Part 5: first and second endings and meter changes (3/4, 6/8) were added to the suggested repeat expansion; infinite repetition is a section that plays inside itself and raises ValueError.
